items.title: Humanity
items.moral: Moral: A profession tells us what someone does; kindness shows who they are. One act of compassion can inspire generations.
body: Kamal had studied hard for years. At last, the day of the exam that would shape his future arrived. His father, Kazim, was demanding and followed his progress closely. He was certain his son would succeed.
Kamal found his exam room. Nervous at first, he relaxed when he read the questions. He answered them easily and felt sure he had done well. With half an hour left, he glanced toward the window.
Something outside caught his attention. Without hesitation, he jumped up and ran for the door.
“Come back!” the examiner called. “If you leave, your exam will be invalid. You’ll lose a whole year!” But Kamal kept running and left through the back door.

When Kazim came home a few hours later, he scolded his son and slapped him. He demanded to know why Kamal had abandoned the exam. Kamal stayed silent, certain that an explanation would only make his father angrier.
For the rest of the year, Kazim repeatedly reproached him. Hurt but quiet, Kamal kept his head down and continued studying.

The next year, he passed and entered medical school. He became an excellent doctor. Although he had lived in the city for years, he volunteered to work at a remote village hospital. A year later, his family came to visit. By then, the quarrel over the exam seemed long forgotten.

One snowy evening, the telephone rang. Someone in a nearby village needed a doctor. Kamal took his bag, and Kazim insisted on accompanying him along the mountain roads. After an hour through the blizzard, they reached the house. An older man opened the door and led them to his sick wife.

Kamal examined her and arranged treatment. She thanked him in a trembling voice. “You came all this way in the cold, my son. What would the world be without people like you? Being truly human isn’t easy. Let me tell you something.

“Years ago, I was in the city when I was suddenly overcome by severe pain. The streets were empty—there was an exam that day. A young man rushed over and helped me to the hospital. It took half an hour in the heat. I was pregnant and terrified for my child. The doctor said that ten minutes later might have been too late for me. My son was born that day.
“The young man told me his name was Kamal. ‘I saw you through the exam-room window,’ he said. ‘You were alone, so I came to help. I’ve lost a year, but I don’t regret it.’

“I named my son Kamal and raised him on that story. Now he is a teacher, and he tries above all to teach his students humanity. I wish I could find that young man and tell him what I owe him. Anyone can become a doctor, a teacher, or an engineer. The hardest thing is to be a good human being. He did not leave me alone in the road.” Dr. Kamal answered softly, “You owe me nothing, Mother. Be at peace.”
Kazim tried to hide his tears. But once they left, they streamed down his face. “Kamal, my son,” he began, and could say no more.

items.title: The Mother-of-Pearl Flower
items.moral: Moral: Love is sometimes expressed through years of quiet care. Recognize that care, and remember to speak gently to those you love.
body: An elderly couple, both in their eighties, stood before a divorce court after fifty years of marriage. The woman’s eyes were swollen from crying. The judge gently asked:
“Why do you want a divorce?”
After taking a deep breath, the old woman began to speak in a choked voice:
“He has worn me down,” she said, her voice breaking. “For fifty years, he has made me weary of life.”

The courtroom fell silent, interrupted only by a photographer’s flash. Reporters waited to hear what she would say. “I have a mother-of-pearl plant that I love dearly. I grew it from a leaf taken from flowers he gave me fifty years ago. We never had children, so I cared for it like a child. One day, it began to wither.

“I promised to get up before dawn every night to water it. In fifty years, he never once offered to do it for me. Last night, I was so exhausted that I couldn’t wake up. I’ve given this man my life, my hopes, everything, and received nothing in return. I would be better off alone.”
The judge turned to the elder:
“Would you like to say anything?”
Leaning on his cane, the husband began:

“I was a gardener during my military service. That was where I met Fatima. I used to bring her the finest flowers I could grow. Soon after we married, she developed neck pain. A doctor told us that sleeping too long without moving made it worse. He advised her to get up and walk around during the night, but she wouldn’t listen to either of us. Then the plant began to wither. I told her it would recover if she got up at night to water it. She promised she would.
“Every night, I woke her and watched her tend the plant she loved like a child. Seeing her care for it, I felt as though I were that flower.”
He paused, then continued:

“After she went back to bed, I got up to empty the excess water from the pot. The plant didn’t need all that water, Your Honor. Last night, I failed to wake too. We’re getting old. Missing its water wouldn’t harm the plant, but I worried about my wife. She blamed me for not waking her. I didn’t argue.”
At that moment everyone in the hall, including the journalists, was in tears…

items.title: Do You Remember Me?
items.moral: Moral: To protect a person’s dignity without shaming them — by closing your eyes — is true teaching. A person whose dignity is kept learns from the mistake and rises.
body: “Hello! Do you remember me? You taught me at school.”
“Yes, in primary school. How good to see you after so many years. What do you do now?”
“I’m a teacher, like you.”
“Wonderful. What made you choose teaching?”
“You did. I wanted to help children grow and find confidence, as you helped me.”
“I’m glad to hear that. Was there something in particular?”

“One boy in our class had a beautiful watch. My parents couldn’t afford one, and I wanted it badly. During a break, I stole it from his pocket. When he reported it missing, you asked for it back. No one answered. You closed the door and told all the boys you would search their pockets. I thought my life was over.

“You lined us up and asked us to cover our eyes. After finding the watch in my pocket, you kept searching everyone else. Then you returned it without saying who had taken it. You never mentioned it to me or my parents. You let me learn from what I’d done without being labeled a thief for the rest of my childhood.
“That taught me what a teacher can be: someone who guides a child through a mistake while protecting their dignity. I decided to become that kind of teacher.”
The teacher listened and was astonished. The young man asked:
“Don’t you remember finding the watch in my pocket?”
“I remember the incident, but I didn’t know you had taken it.”
“How could you not know? You found it yourself!”
“I had closed my eyes too.”

items.title: Three Questions
items.moral: Moral: Position is never permanent. Remember that circumstances can change, and remain humble.
body: The king called the vizier to him and said:
“Answer three questions by tomorrow or leave the palace. What does Allah patiently bear? What does He conceal? And what does He bring about through His wisdom and power?”
The vizier thought hard but found no answers. He returned home in despair. His clever servant noticed his distress and asked what was wrong.
The servant said:
“I know the answers,” the servant said. “I’ll give you two now and the third tomorrow. Allah bears His servants’ sorrows and conceals their faults.”
The next day, the vizier went to the king and told him these two answers. The king said:
“Correct. Did you think of these answers yourself?”
The vizier answered honestly:
“My servant taught me.”
The king ordered the vizier to hand his robe to the servant. The two exchanged clothes and positions.
Stunned, the former vizier asked:
“And the third answer? What does Allah bring about through His wisdom and power?”
The servant smiled.
“Haven’t you seen? In a moment, He can make a vizier a servant and a servant a vizier.”

items.title: Compassion
items.moral: Moral: Compassion gives humanity its meaning. It means more than sharing someone’s tears; it means looking for a way to ease their suffering.
body: It was a cold winter night, and I was walking home from work. Ahead of me, a man was swaying and clinging weakly to a lamppost. He looked drunk. As I approached, I saw that he was in his thirties, clean and neatly dressed. Some passersby made loud remarks about the dangers of alcohol; others laughed at him.
“Are you all right? Do you need help?” I asked.
His answer came out as a groan.
“I’m ill.”

I put an arm around his waist to steady him and helped him to a taxi stand. The snow, which had stopped earlier that evening, was falling again. The only movement on the empty streets came from stray dogs chasing one another across the freezing roads.
I was beginning to give up hope when a taxi pulled up. I explained what had happened and told the driver we needed to hurry.
We settled the man in the back seat and drove to the hospital. The doctors treated him immediately and gave him medication. The driver and I waited at his bedside.
The doctor on duty told us that, at the very least, we had saved him from freezing. Still unable to speak, the man looked at us and smiled. When he recovered enough to leave, we drove him home.
His wife knew that he was prone to diabetic comas. Terrified, she had gone out to look for him with their son. When they saw us, they rushed over. The family embraced, their eyes shining with joy.
After hours of worry, our tiredness vanished. The family could not find words to thank us, and their happiness became our own.
When we said goodbye, I asked the driver what I owed him.
He shook his head:

“You owe me nothing, my friend. I’m the one who owes you,” he said. “You let me share in something good. I had almost forgotten how it felt to cry—it must have been twenty years. Thank you for reminding me.”
I hugged the driver and set off home on foot, no longer feeling the night’s cold.
Who knew? Perhaps I would meet someone else who needed help along the way.

items.title: Training or Nature?
items.moral: Moral: Training may shape behavior, but an opportunity can reveal the nature beneath it. Learning matters, but character matters too.
body: A king asked his minister:
“Which matters more: training or nature?”
The minister answered without hesitation:
“Nature, Your Majesty.”
The king ordered his subjects to find the finest animal trainer in the country. When the man was brought before him, the king asked:
“How long would it take you to teach a cat to serve guests with a bowl in its paw?”
“Six months, Your Majesty.”
Six months later, the trainer returned to the palace with the cat.
“Have you taught it?” the king asked.
“Yes, Your Majesty.”
The court gathered, and the cat began serving the guests. As it approached the minister, the king asked again:
“Which matters more: training or nature?”
Before answering, the minister took a mouse from his pocket and released it. The cat immediately dropped the bowl and chased it.
Then the minister turned to the king.
“Nature, Your Majesty.”

items.title: A Glass of Milk
items.moral: Moral: A selfless act of kindness is never lost. It is entered into an unseen account and may return to us one day—often when we least expect it.
body: A poor boy who sold small goods from door to door to pay his tuition discovered one day that he had no money left and was desperately hungry. He decided to knock on the next door and ask for something to eat.

A young woman answered. Embarrassed, the boy could not bring himself to ask for food and requested only a glass of water. Seeing that he was hungry, the woman brought him a large glass of milk instead.
After drinking it slowly, the boy asked:
“How much do I owe you?”
“Nothing,” she replied. “My mother taught us to be kind without expecting anything in return.”
The boy could say only:
“Thank you from the bottom of my heart.”
As he walked away, he felt stronger not only physically, but also in spirit. His faith in God and in other people had been renewed.
Years passed. One day, the same woman became seriously ill. Unable to determine the cause of her illness, the local doctors sent her to specialists in a large city.

Dr. Howard Kelly was called in for a consultation. When he heard which town the patient came from, he immediately went to her room. The moment he saw her, he recognized the woman who had given him a glass of milk years before and rekindled hope in his heart.
Dr. Kelly personally took charge of her treatment and resolved to do everything he could to save her. After a long struggle, the illness was overcome and the woman recovered.
When the time came for her discharge, Dr. Kelly requested the final bill. He wrote a few words along its edge and had it delivered to the patient’s room.
The woman opened it anxiously. She feared that she would never be able to pay the amount and would spend the rest of her life repaying the debt. Then she noticed a sentence written in the margin:
“Paid in full with one glass of milk.”
Signed: Dr. Howard Kelly.

TITLE: A Glass of Milk
BODY[1]: A poor boy who sold small goods from door to door to pay his tuition discovered one day that he had no money left and was desperately hungry. He decided to knock on the next door and ask for something to eat.
BODY[2]: A young woman answered. Embarrassed, the boy could not bring himself to ask for food and requested only a glass of water. Seeing that he was hungry, the woman brought him a large glass of milk instead.
BODY[3]: After drinking it slowly, the boy asked:
BODY[4]: “How much do I owe you?”
BODY[5]: “Nothing,” she replied. “My mother taught us to be kind without expecting anything in return.”
BODY[6]: The boy could say only:
BODY[7]: “Thank you from the bottom of my heart.”
BODY[8]: As he walked away, he felt stronger not only physically, but also in spirit. His faith in God and in other people had been renewed.
BODY[9]: Years passed. One day, the same woman became seriously ill. Unable to determine the cause of her illness, the local doctors sent her to specialists in a large city.
BODY[10]: Dr. Howard Kelly was called in for a consultation. When he heard which town the patient came from, he immediately went to her room. The moment he saw her, he recognized the woman who had given him a glass of milk years before and rekindled hope in his heart.
BODY[11]: Dr. Kelly personally took charge of her treatment and resolved to do everything he could to save her. After a long struggle, the illness was overcome and the woman recovered.
BODY[12]: When the time came for her discharge, Dr. Kelly requested the final bill. He wrote a few words along its edge and had it delivered to the patient’s room.
BODY[13]: The woman opened it anxiously. She feared that she would never be able to pay the amount and would spend the rest of her life repaying the debt. Then she noticed a sentence written in the margin:
BODY[14]: “Paid in full with one glass of milk.”
BODY[15]: Signed: Dr. Howard Kelly.
MORAL: Moral: A selfless act of kindness is never lost. It is entered into an unseen account and may return to us one day—often when we least expect it.

items.title: Knowing When to Walk Away
items.moral: Moral: Stepping back from people who disregard your values can be an act of self-respect.
body: There is dignity in walking away:
from those who value nothing,
those who trample on sincerity,
those who abandon their principles for gain,
from arrogant and boastful people,
those who are envious, gossipers,
those who make a habit of lying,
those who do not know what decency is,
those who betray their values,
those who turn a blind eye to ignorance,
those who despise their homeland, deny their nation,
those who forget their native language,
those who show no love or respect for parents and children.
There is dignity in walking away
from those who believe they cannot be replaced.
